vm.app.title: Virtual Machine
vm.app.subtitle: Windows and Linux desktop VMs
vm.welcome.title: Welcome to Virtual Machine
vm.welcome.lead: Run Windows and Linux desktops at near-native speed on Apple silicon. Shared host folders, two-way clipboard and automatic resolution on window resize all work out of the box.
vm.welcome.createDesc: Pick a guest system, assign CPU and memory, attach an installer image and start installing within a minute.
vm.empty.title: No machines yet
vm.empty.lead: Use “New machine” in the top right to create one, or import an existing image.
vm.list.noSelection: Select a machine on the left
vm.create.title: New machine
vm.create.name: Name
vm.create.archHint: Only arm64 guests can use native virtualization on Apple silicon; x86_64 requires QEMU emulation and is slow.
vm.create.diskHint: Created as a sparse file, so it only takes real space as the guest writes.
vm.create.storageDirHint: Only the disk moves here; metadata stays in the default folder so the VM stays in the list.
vm.create.storageLow: Not enough space: {free} GB free, {need} GB needed.
vm.create.installerHint: Pick an ISO, or leave empty to boot straight from the system disk.
vm.create.sharedDirsHint: 9p works out of the box on Linux guests; virtio-fs is faster but needs virtiofsd on a Linux host; SMB uses the host file service so Windows guests need no driver.
vm.settings.title: Machine settings
vm.settings.clipboardHint: The guest needs spice-vdagent (Linux) or spice-guest-tools (Windows).
vm.settings.autoResizeHint: Pushes the new display mode to the guest while you resize the window.
vm.rosetta.label: Rosetta (x86_64 translation)
vm.rosetta.hint: Lets a Linux guest run x86_64 binaries without switching guest architecture.
vm.rosetta.notInstalled: Rosetta is not installed. Run softwareupdate --install-rosetta in a terminal, then restart the host app.
vm.rosetta.notSupported: Rosetta is not supported on this host (Apple silicon required).
vm.console.waitingHint: Press “Start” above and the guest screen shows up here.
vm.console.agentHint: If the clipboard does not work, install spice-vdagent inside the guest.
vm.console.engineFallback: The current engine cannot embed the screen; the VM runs in QEMU's own window.
vm.console.mountHint: Inside the guest run: mount -t 9p -o trans=virtio {tag} /mnt/{tag}
vm.console.clipboardHint: Two-way clipboard is on; copying needs spice-vdagent inside the guest.
vm.console.detached: Screen detached into its own window
vm.delete.confirmDetail: “{name}” and its disk image will be removed permanently.
vm.error.load: Failed to load the machine list
vm.error.noEngine: No virtualization engine is available on this system
vm.error.desktopOnly: Virtual machines require the OTools desktop app. A browser has no virtualization capability, so machines cannot be created or started here.
vm.error.hostOutdated: This build of OTools lacks the virtualization entitlement. Update OTools to {version} or later before starting a virtual machine.
vm.clone.title: Clone machine
vm.clone.hint: Uses copy-on-write on APFS: completes in seconds and takes almost no extra space until the new machine actually writes.
vm.resize.title: Resize disk
vm.resize.hint: Growing only — shrinking would destroy guest data. Afterwards extend the partition and filesystem inside the guest: growpart + resize2fs on Linux, “Extend Volume” in Windows Disk Management.
vm.snapshot.saveHint: Save the whole machine (including memory) to disk and stop it; survives closing the app or rebooting, pick up with Resume
vm.snapshot.restoreHint: Resume from the suspended state (works even after closing the app or rebooting)
vm.snapshot.unsupported: Suspend is not supported for this configuration
vm.console.suspendedHint: The machine is paused and saved to disk. Click Resume to continue — closing OTools or rebooting is fine.
vm.create.firmwareHint: Modern systems like Windows 11 require UEFI; ignored on macOS / arm64 hosts.
vm.create.driverIsoHint: e.g. virtio-win; lets Windows Setup detect the virtio disk/NIC via "Load driver".
vm.engine.softwareAccel: Running under QEMU software emulation (no hardware acceleration) — slower. On Windows hosts, enable "Windows Hypervisor Platform" and restart to speed up.
vm.engine.prefSaved: Engine preference saved; restart the plugin to apply
vm.share.protocol9p: 9p · works on Linux out of the box
vm.share.virtiofsUnsupported: virtio-fs needs a Linux host with virtiofsd, which this host does not provide. Use 9p instead.
vm.console.mountHintVirtiofs: Inside the guest run: mount -t virtiofs {tag} /mnt/{tag} (Linux); virtiofs.exe -m Z: -t {tag} (Windows)
vm.settings.virtiofsdHint: Only needed for the virtio-fs protocol. Install: Fedora dnf install virtiofsd; Debian/Ubuntu apt install virtiofsd.
vm.device.title: Devices & boot
vm.device.bootOrderEmpty: No boot order configured; using the QEMU default.
vm.device.bootOrderHint: Firmware tries each device in order. Note: SeaBIOS allows only one disk to boot, so the first disk in the list is the one that counts.
vm.device.addBootItem: Choose a boot device to add
vm.device.usbMediaHint: Attached as a USB mass-storage device, so it shows up as a USB drive inside the guest. Add "USB drive" to the boot order to boot from it.
vm.device.portForwardsHint: Maps a host port into the guest, e.g. 3389 for Remote Desktop. Bound to 127.0.0.1 by default, so it is not exposed to the LAN.
vm.device.portDuplicate: Only one rule per protocol and host port
vm.net.title: Network
vm.net.modeNatHint: The guest reaches the internet and host through a virtual gateway. No administrator rights, works out of the box; use port forwarding below for host-to-guest access.
vm.net.modeBridgedHint: The guest joins the host LAN with a real address on the same subnet, so other devices on the network can reach it directly.
vm.net.modeHostOnlyHint: The guest talks only to the host and stays off the network. Good for isolated environments or internal testing.
vm.net.interfacePlaceholder: Pick an adapter, or type a name
vm.net.interfaceHint: The guest joins the network through this adapter. Connected adapters are listed automatically.
vm.net.interfaceEmpty: No connected adapter detected. Please type the adapter name.
vm.net.interfaceWireless: This is a wireless adapter; bridging it adds jitter. Prefer a wired adapter when stability matters.
vm.net.portForwardNatOnly: Port forwarding only applies to Shared (NAT). Bridged and host-only guests already have their own address.
vm.net.hostShareHint: Pick the SMB protocol for a folder under Sharing and the guest can open the path below directly, with no driver required in the guest.
vm.share.smbHint: Served by the host file service; Windows guests need no driver.
vm.console.mountHintSmb: In the guest: net use Z: \\{host}\{name} (or open the path in Explorer)
vm.console.noDisplayHint: The HCS engine has no display output API. The VM keeps running in the background but its desktop is not visible. Use the QEMU backend when you need a screen.
vm.console.noDisplayFoot: HCS has no display API: the VM is still running and can be stopped or paused
vm.hcs.title: HCS engine
vm.hcs.reasonElevation: Run OTools as administrator to use HCS; otherwise QEMU is used
vm.hcs.reasonComponent: Enable “Virtual Machine Platform” in Windows Features and reboot
vm.hcs.diskVhdx: HCS only supports VHDX disks; RAW disks are converted automatically on start
vm.qemu.title: QEMU is not installed
vm.qemu.lead: QEMU can be fetched in one click — no website, no PATH setup.
vm.qemu.manualLead: This system needs a manual install.
vm.hcs.orphanTitle: Leftover virtual machines are still running
vm.hcs.orphanLead: {count} virtual machine(s) were left behind when the host exited unexpectedly. They are not listed on the left but still hold memory and disk files. You can clean them up here.
vm.hcs.orphanPartial: Cleaned up {done}, but {rest} could not be stopped. Retry or restart the system.
vm.settings.liveMemory: The VM is running: only memory can be changed here. Power it off to edit anything else.
vm.settings.liveReadonly: The VM is running and the current engine cannot change settings live. Power it off first.
